docs/AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md:1566:Worktree preflight refuses non-git sources, repos with no commits, detached HEAD, mid-merge, mid-rebase, dirty trees unless `--allow-dirty`, branch collisions, and occupied worktree paths. Errors include `try:` lines.
docs/AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md:1631:After every successful tool/provider turn, `crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs` calls the turn-end documentation checkpoint. The deterministic record lands in `_incremental.jsonl`, rewrites the Markdown drafts, projects current `implementation-notes.html` sections into `RUN-DECISIONS.md`, and emits a `docs_checkpoint` run event before the loop advances. This happens for both CLI sub-agent turns that complete in one provider process and JSON-action providers that may take many Bash/WriteFile/Done turns.
docs/AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md:1715:Output and scripting flags have a visible policy in `deadreckon help-all`. `--yes` confirms preflight previews for start/update-style commands. `--no-confirm` skips destructive or follow-up confirmations after the target is known. `--quiet` suppresses success chatter and post-action hints, never requested data or errors. `--plain` disables TUI, spinner, and ANSI affordances without implying quiet. `--json` is reserved for inspection/list surfaces and wins over styling and hints. `--no-hints` suppresses optional next-step hints; `DEADRECKON_HINTS=0|false|off|no` disables them globally for the process.
docs/AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md:1723:The user-facing skip model is split by timing. `--yes` belongs to preflight preview acceptance on commands such as `run`, `orchestrate`, `chain`, and shell-channel `update`; `--no-confirm` belongs to direct destructive or follow-up actions such as `finish`, `apply`, `cleanup`, chain recovery commands, and doc polish.
docs/AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md:1739:Done-criteria setup also resolves through `setup.rs`. Explicit `--acceptance <path>`, project `.deadreckon/acceptance.yaml`, generated criteria from `def-done`/pre-run drafting, and default `dr-gate` behavior all produce one `DoneCriteriaSelection`. User-facing previews and orchestration preflights say `done criteria`; technical files, gate proofs, and hidden compatibility commands may still say `acceptance.yaml` or `gate`.
docs/AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md:1929:- `orchestrate review <goal>` and `orchestrate full-plan <goal>` are the one-command wrappers. Both print a preflight with mode, provider role table, dependency/parallelism summary, sandbox, caps, capabilities, merge-repair posture, and task rows before starting child work; headless callers pass `--yes`, `--preview` writes the plan and stops before `fork`, and automatic merge repair stays enabled unless an advanced/debug caller passes `--no-repair`.

    20	    let run_id = run_id.ok_or("--run is required")?;
    21	    let working_dir = working_dir.ok_or("--working-dir is required")?;
    22	    let run_root = match run_root {
    23	        Some(run_root) => run_root,
    24	        None => infer_run_root(&working_dir)?,
    25	    };
    26	    let results = evaluate_acceptance_checks_with_progress(&run_root, &working_dir)?;
    27	    if let Some(failed) = results
    28	        .iter()
    29	        .find(|result| result.must_pass && !result.passed)
    30	    {
    31	        eprintln!("acceptance failed");
    32	        for result in &results {
    33	            let mark = if result.passed { "PASS" } else { "FAIL" };
    34	            let required = if result.must_pass {
    35	                "required"
    36	            } else {
    37	                "optional"
    38	            };
    39	            eprintln!("{mark} {required} {}: {}", result.kind, result.detail);
    40	            if !result.passed {
    41	                if let Some(stderr) = result.stderr.as_deref() {
    42	                    eprintln!("stderr: {}", one_line(stderr, 500));
    43	                }
    44	                if let Some(stdout) = result.stdout.as_deref() {
    45	                    eprintln!("stdout: {}", one_line(stdout, 500));
    46	                }
    47	            }
    48	        }
    49	        return Err(format!("required check failed: {}", failed.detail).into());
    50	    }
    51	    write_acceptance_marker_with_results(&run_root, run_id, working_dir, results)?;
    52	    Ok(())
    53	}

    55	fn one_line(value: &str, limit: usize) -> String {
    56	    let compact = value.split_whitespace().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(" ");
    57	    if compact.len() <= limit {
    58	        compact
    59	    } else {
    60	        let clipped = compact.chars().take(limit).collect::<String>();
    61	        format!("{clipped}...")
    62	    }
    63	}

    65	fn infer_run_root(working_dir: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    66	    if working_dir.file_name().and_then(|name| name.to_str()) != Some("working") {
    67	        return Err("working directory must be <run-root>/working".into());
    68	    }
    69	    working_dir
    70	        .parent()
    71	        .map(Path::to_path_buf)
    72	        .ok_or_else(|| "working directory has no parent".into())
    73	}

    52	deadreckon is a Rust 2024 CLI harness whose default flow is **unattended long-running coding tasks**: `deadreckon run <goal>` creates durable run state, picks a BYOK provider route, executes turns inside a platform-native sandbox, writes spend/provenance/trace records after every turn, and exits only when the LLM declares done, a budget caps the run, or the operator kills it. The CLI is the user-facing layer; `deadreckon-runtime` owns orchestration across providers, sandboxes, docs, and promotion; `deadreckon-core` owns deterministic primitives and durable schemas.

     2	
     3	**Status:** Design

     6	
     7	## TL;DR
     8	
     9	Deadreckon ships descriptor-backed support for two CLI agent providers today
    10	(`cli:claude-code`, `cli:codex`). The recent commits `6bdafe2 → fe0297a → 1af0778`
    11	moved provider identity, sandbox paths, model catalogs, and `dr detect` probing
    12	into TOML descriptors. **Detection, launch, and sandboxing are now generalized.
    13	Log ingest is not** — the TUI activity feed and the per-provider parsers are
    14	still a hand-coded two-arm match on `ProviderJsonlSchema { CodexCli, ClaudeCode }`.
    15	
    16	Meanwhile, `agentsview` already has a parser registry covering **24 agents** with
    17	a uniform `AgentDef` shape, a canonical tool-category taxonomy, and per-agent
    18	session-discovery functions. This doc maps what we'd need to extend the
    19	descriptor schema and refactor the JSONL pipeline so that adding a third CLI
    20	provider (e.g. `cli:gemini`) requires **one TOML file plus one parser variant**
    21	rather than ~15 new match arms.
    22	
    23	## 1. Two registries, one identity layer
    24	
    25	Deadreckon and agentsview already converge on most of the same identity fields.
    26	They diverge after that because they have different jobs.
    27	
    28	| Concern | deadreckon (this repo) | agentsview |
    29	|---|---|---|
    30	| Identify the agent | `ProviderDescriptor.id` | `AgentDef.Type` |
    31	| Display name | `display_name` | `DisplayName` |
    32	| Default state dirs | `fs_detection_paths` | `DefaultDirs` |
    33	| Env var override | — *(missing)* | `EnvVar` |
    34	| ID prefix for namespacing | — *(missing)* | `IDPrefix` |
    35	| Watched subdirs | — *(missing)* | `WatchSubdirs`, `ShallowWatch` |
    36	| Launch (binary, args, model) | `default_binary`, `exec_template`, `model_arg` | n/a |
    37	| Auth + sandbox + version probe | `auth`, `sandbox_writes`, `version_probe` | n/a |
    38	| Install hint | `install_hint`, `try_lines` | n/a |
    39	| Session-file discovery | hard-coded for codex/claude in `main.rs` | `DiscoverFunc` / `FindSourceFunc` |
    40	| Parse JSONL → activity lines | hard-coded `codex_activity_line` / `claude_activity_lines` | per-agent parser + canonical `ParsedSession` / `ParsedMessage` |
    41	| Tool name normalization | — | `NormalizeToolCategory` (single switch, 100+ raw names → 9 categories) |
    42	
    43	The two registries are **complementary, not redundant**. Treat agentsview as
    44	prior art for the *post-run* side of the descriptor (discover, parse, classify)

Phase progression is explicit, with only phase 60 mapping to completed status in [state.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/state.rs:150). Run roots, current pointers, plans, chains, worker specs, summaries, merge proofs, conductor state, and library paths are centralized in [paths.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/paths.rs:34).

- **Durability/locking:** State writes and JSONL appends are atomic/synced in [state.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/state.rs:435). Per-workspace locks include stale/PID handling and heartbeat support in [lock.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/lock.rs:91). Promotion validates the gate, recovers run state, stages atomically, and records provenance hash in [promotion.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/promotion.rs:27).

- **Traces/provenance/events:** Spend, provenance, and trace JSONL records are first-class append-only artifacts in [artifacts.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/artifacts.rs:11). Run events cover turns, tools, token/spend deltas, docs checkpoints, completion, promotion, and errors in [events.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/events.rs:10). The turn loop records LLM traces/spend, tool provenance, and reconstructs history from traces in [turn_loop.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs:221) and [turn_loop.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs:1084).

- **Docs/goals/riders:** The default coding skill clearly separates binary-owned state/sandbox/provenance/gates from agent-owned judgment/docs in [SKILL.md](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/skills/default-coding/SKILL.md:13). Runtime docs produce narrative, as-built, decisions, incremental JSONL, polish metadata, and implementation notes in [docs.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/docs.rs:178). Docs freshness is enforced by implementation-notes checks in [docs.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/docs.rs:482) and by corrective turn-loop feedback in [turn_loop.rs](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs:1309). The strongest self-improving loop is already present as: durable runstate + append-only traces/provenance/events + docs checkpoints + provider ingest/flight checkpoints + external gate feedback + promotion/rewind + plan/chain orchestration.
